Monica / Redwood team,

Thanks for taking a look — we're finalizing the deployment checklist for a small footprint private cluster at our Chattanooga micro-site (EdgeFleet Logistics). High level items we need your guidance on and confirmation so procurement can sign off: 

- Expected persistent storage profile: 8-12 TB total per rack, primary workload is inference KV store + local disk-backed caches (low-latency writes, high read concurrency).
- Requirement: local NVMe on inference nodes for KV cache with replication to at-rest medium-term archival (S3-compatible).
- Network: isolated VLANs per tenant, BGP eBGP peering to our edge router, explicit egress IPs for outbound model telemetry.
- HA: tolerates single-node failure within a rack; cross-rack failover acceptable but prefer async replication for local caches.
- Security: we must be able to bring our own KMS and have audit logs for token usage for 90 days.

Attached is a short inventory and our initial IO expectations (see edgefleet-topology-v1.pdf). Can you outline the node-class mix you recommend, minimal PV class configuration, and any gating items we should surface to our facilities team? We want a clear mutual action plan and an estimate of onboarding time so we can align procurement timelines.

Best,
Sam Turner
Dir. Infrastructure Ops, EdgeFleet Logistics

Sam — thanks, useful inventory. Leaning here on a compact design to meet your HA and IO goals without over-provisioning. Proposed mutual action plan below (30-min technical review -> preflight checklist -> staging run -> go/no-go):

1) Suggested node classes (initial landing):
   - control-plane: 3x m-class (cpu-optimized, 3 masters across two racks if possible).
   - inference-cache: 2x high-IO NVMe nodes (local NVMe 8TB each), tainted for inference workloads, heartbeats to local monitoring.
   - storage-replica: 2x medium NVMe + 24TB SATA for medium-term archive (object gateway + scheduled replication).
   - burst-worker (optional): 1-2 GPU-capable nodes if you plan model fine-tuning at edge (can be added later).

2) PV strategy and classes:
   - pv-class: fast-local-nvme (localPV, ReadWriteOnce, no bind to scheduler except node affinity). Use a small explicit eviction threshold (e.g., 80% usage) and set kubelet reserved disk.
   - pv-class: replicated-archive (blockstore backed by network-attached storage or object gateway). Snapshot schedule to central S3 nightly.
   - Suggest prefix/KV cache use tmpfs or ephemeral SSD with periodic flush to local NVMe for durability.

3) Networking and peering notes:
   - We'll recommend dedicated VLANs per tenant plus BGP eBGP peering to your edge router. Egress IPs can be static via NAT gateway we configure in conjunction with your network team.

4) Security & compliance gating:
   - Redwood can integrate with your KMS for model keys and we can expose token audit logs (90 days). Need a short onboarding ticket for KMS credentials exchange.

5) Next steps / ask:
   - Can your facilities confirm: 1) two top-of-rack switch uplinks to separate aggregation switches, 2) physical rack power per node class?
   - Suggested calendar: 30-min technical sync on 2026-09-01 at 10:00 AM ET.

I've attached an initial IO estimate (io-capacity-estimate.xlsx) and a lightweight topology. Irene and Laura: can you add any kernel/tuning or operational concerns? Karthik, I'll leave commercial notes to you re: committed capacity and timeline.

Thanks — Monica

Quick tech addendum from SRE perspective — a few actionable items to avoid surprise IO behavior during steady-state: 

- IO profile: serve-heavy reads with short hot windows. Recommend write-intent WAL on local NVMe, then async ship to replicated-archive. Avoid host-level RAID that masks device failures — prefer localPV + application replication.
- Filesystem & mount opts: use XFS with noatime, barrier=1 where supported. Mount with nodiratime; tune rcu and irq affinity if you see network CPU contention.
- Kernel tuning: increase nr_requests and elevator_mq parameters for NVMe; set read_ahead_kb to 256 for larger sequential reads, but keep it conservative for KV workloads.
- Kube settings: set kubelet evictionHard: memory.available<200Mi,disk.available<10% (adjust after staging), and set Topology Aware Hints for kube-proxy to reduce cross-rack pod hop.
- PersistentVolume consideration: for localPV, add nodeAffinity with a label like node.kubernetes.io/nvme=true and tolerations for inference taint. Use a small dynamic-provisioning shim if you need thin provisioning for future growth.

Operational risk: if a single NVMe node fails, expect a brief cache rebuild; ensure your app supports an eventual-consistent fallback to central object storage. We should run a simulated node-failure exercise in staging.

I'll bring a short checklist for the sync on Sep 1.

— Irene
